citation.authors: Hori A, Sobue S, Kurokawa R, Hirano S, Ichihara M, Hotta N
citation.title: Two-week continuous supplementation of hydrogen-rich water increases peak oxygen uptake during an incremental cycling exercise test in healthy humans: a randomized, single-blinded, placebo-controlled study (rest values of the placebo trial read)

population.description: Nine healthy university students (6 men, 3 women), Experiment 1; age 19.9 ± 0.4 y (mean ± SE), height 169.6 ± 3.0 cm, weight 63.7 ± 4.1 kg (Table 1). Age SD = SE x sqrt(9) = 1.2, computed here. BMI is not printed.

protocols.name: pw_rest
protocols.description: Placebo-water (PW) trial of Experiment 1, pre-exercise rest only. The participants drank 500 mL of placebo water (entered as no meal), sat for 30 min, then (Methods) rested 5 min on the ergometer with a respiratory mask before a 3 min warm-up at 0 W; the paper does not say whether that 5 min is inside the 30 min of seated rest, so the Table 2 rest values are entered as the mean over minutes 25-30 of a 30-minute arm. The exercise itself (ramp +20 W per min to exhaustion) is not entered. The paper says nothing about food before the visit or the time of day, so no fast and no meal are assumed: the arm starts from typical values (norm_center) and the clock hour is assumed.
